1.note: A **wilderness** is a kind of dry, remote, uncultivated area. If your readers would not be familiar with what a wilderness is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [in the barren region of Sinai] or [in the remote desert of Sinai]
The implication is that **one** means “the first day” of the second month. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the first day]

The word **one** here means “first.” Hebrew sometimes uses cardinal numbers (1, 2, 3) where other languages would use ordinal numbers (first, second, third). If your language does not use cardinal numbers this way, you can use an ordinal number instead.

The **second month** of the Hebrew calendar includes the last half of April and the first half of May on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar, which is “Iyar” here, then say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

The words **second month** and **second year** use ordinal numbers (first, second, third). Some languages use cardinal numbers (1, 2, 3) in these situations. If your language does not use ordinal numbers this way, you can use cardinal numbers instead.

Here and throughout this chapter, the term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. For more information, see the book introduction.

2.note: The phrase **Lift up the head of** is a common expression of this culture to mean “count” or “take a census of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [count the number of] or [record the total of]
The command **Lift up** is plural here because God is speaking to both Moses and Aaron. So use the plural form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that **all** refers specifically to the men, as shown later in the verse by “every male.” You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [all the men of]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by being **the sons of Israel**. If your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the congregation that consists of the sons of Israel]

This is the first of many times in this book that **sons of Israel** refers to the Israelite nation or people group who descended from **Israel**. See the discussion of how to translate this phrase in the book introduction.

Here and throughout this chapter, the phrase **house of their fathers** refers to largest divisions within a single tribe. The word **clans** refers to the largest divisions of each **house of their fathers**. Alternate translation: [according to their clans, according to the house of their fathers made up of those clans]
Here, **house** refers to people who are related. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to the family groups of]
Yahweh is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [their ancestors]

The implication is that Moses was to write down the name of each man as he counted them, creating a list or record. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by listing the names of each one counted]

Yahweh is using **skulls** to represent whole persons. He means that each person should be counted only one time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [counting each person] or [one by one]

3.note: Yahweh is using **from a son of 20 years and upward** as a common expression of his culture to mean “any male who is at least 20 years old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [who are twenty years old or older] or [aged twenty and above]

The implication is that these men are able to serve as soldiers and fight in battle. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [who is able to serve in the army] or [who is fit for military service]
Here, **Israel** refers to the Israelite nation or people group. See the discussion of how to translate **Israel** in the book introduction.
The word **you** is singular here because Yahweh is speaking to Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that each tribe was organized and arranged into military units or divisions. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [by their military divisions]

4.note: The implication is that these men will be helping Moses and Aaron with the task of counting the people. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [To assist you in this task] or [Working together with you]
Since Yahweh is speaking to both Moses and Aaron, the form of **you** would be dual here, if your language uses that form. Otherwise, the word would be plural.

Here, the phrase **will be** is plural, but **man** is singular. The implication is that one man from each tribe will assist Moses and Aaron. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [must each be represented by one man] or [will each send one man]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **man** who belongs to each **tribe**. If your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a man who represents each tribe] or [a man who belongs to each tribe]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if the tribal leader were the **head** of a body. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the chief leader] or [the principal leader]

Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. So the house of the ancestors figuratively means all the people descended from the tribal patriarchs. Alternate translation: [from the clan] or [from the extended family]

Yahweh is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [of his ancestors] or [of his forefathers]

5.note: In this list, the name after **son of** is always the name of a man.

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if helping with the census were actually **standing** with Moses and Aaron. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will help you count the people] or [will assist you with the census]
Since Yahweh is speaking to two people, Moses and Aaron, the form of **you** would be dual here, if your language uses that form. Otherwise, the word would be plural.

Here and in 1:6–15, **of** indicates that the named person (here **Elizur**) is a member of the tribe (in this case, **Reuben**). See the chapter introduction for more information. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different expression. Alternate translation: [from the tribe of Reuben]

15.note: The direct speech that began in 1:2 could: (1) end at the end of this verse. (2) end at the end of 1:16.

16.note: The expression **called ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, it could be: (1) God. Alternate translation: [{were} the ones whom God called from the congregation] (2) the congregation. Alternate translation: [{were} the ones whom the congregation called]

The implication is that these men were appointed or chosen by God for leadership in Israel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [were the chosen ones of]
See how you translated the same use of this phrase in 1:2.
See how you translated the same use of “head” in 1:4.

Here, the author is speaking as if Israel’s tribal divisions were actually **thousands**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the divisions within Israel]

17.q: וַ⁠יִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְ⁠אַהֲרֹ֑ן אֵ֚ת הָ⁠אֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ⁠אֵ֔לֶּה
17.note: Here, the author is speaking as if these men were objects that Moses and Aaron physically **took**. He means that Moses and Aaron gathered these men together. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then Moses and Aaron summoned these men] or [Then Moses and Aaron gathered these men together]

The expression **were designated** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [whom Yahweh had designated]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [by their names]

18.note: See how you translated this phrase in [1:1](ta:01).

Here, **they** could refer to: (1) all the Israelite men who were 20 years old or older. Alternate translation: [And the Israelites recorded their ancestry] (2) Moses and Aaron, while **their** refers to all the Israelites. Alternate translation: [And Moses and Aaron recorded the Israelites’ ancestry]
See how you translated the similar phrases in 1:2.
See how you translated this phrase in 1:2.

20.note: These verses list the number Israelites from each tribe who were above 20 years old and able to fight. See the chapter introduction for information on how to translate these repetitive verses. The following notes give information on verses that include unique elements.

The phrase **and they were** introduces the whole list of names and numbers that follows. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Here is what Moses recorded:]
The word **Israel** is the name of a man, the son of Isaac. The word **Israel** does not refer to the Israelites here. Alternate translation: [Isaac’s son Israel]

The author is using **skulls** to represent whole persons. He means that each person should be counted only one time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [individually]

22.note: See how you translated this phrase in 1:20.

It might seem that the expression **his counted ones** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language, especially since a similar phrase appears in the next verse. If so, you can omit it.

The expression **counted ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [those whom Moses and Aaron counted]

The author is using the possessive form to mean the counted ones who came from Simeon’s tribe. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the counted ones from Simeon]

34.note: The implication is that Manasseh, along with Ephraim, was one of Joseph’s sons. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Also of the sons of Joseph: of the sons of Manasseh]

42.note: Here, the preposition translated **Of** is omitted to indicate that this is the last tribe in the list. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Lastly, of the sons of Naphtali]

44.note: It might seem that the expression **counted ones whom Moses and Aaron had counted** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [were the people whom Moses and Aaron had counted]

Here Moses implies that these **12 men** helped **Moses and Aaron** count the people, as stated in 1:5. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state this explicitly. Alternate translation: [with the 12 leaders of Israel helping them]

The author is using **one man for the house of his fathers** as a common expression of his culture to mean “each person represented his ancestral house.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Each one of them was from the house of his fathers]
Here, **house** means all the people descended from a particular person. It envisions them as if they were one household living together. Alternate translation: [of the household]

The author is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [of his ancestors] or [of his family line]

45.note: The expression **counted ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom Moses, Aaron, and the 12 leaders counted]
See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:44.

45.q: מִ⁠בֶּ֨ן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ וָ⁠מַ֔עְלָ⁠ה כָּל־יֹצֵ֥א צָבָ֖א
45.note: See how you translated these phrases in 1:20–43.

46.note: The expression **counted ones** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the ones whom Moses, Aaron, and the 12 leaders counted]

46.q: שֵׁשׁ־מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֖לֶף וּ⁠שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֑ים וַ⁠חֲמֵ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת וַ⁠חֲמִשִּֽׁים
46.note: See how you translated the large numbers in 1:20–43.

47.note: The author uses the word **And** here to indicate a contrast between what was expected (that the Levites would be counted along with the other tribes) and what actually happened (they were not counted). In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But the Levites]
See how you translated the similar phrase “tribes of their fathers” in 1:16.

The expression **were not counted** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [were those whom Moses, Aaron, and the 12 leaders did not count]

Here, the author is speaking as if including the Levites in the census count meant counting the Levites **in the midst of** the other tribes. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [together with them]

48.note: The word **And** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [The reason for this is that Yahweh spoke]

The previous verse describes how the Levites were not included in the census. If it is helpful in your language, you might want to make it clear that the account that starts in this verse happened before the census was taken. The UST does that by using the phrase “had told.” Alternate translation: [And Yahweh previously spoke]

49.note: The word **you** is singular here because God is speaking directly to Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:2.
See how you translated the similar phrase in 1:47.

50.note: The word **you** is singular here because God is speaking directly to Moses. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that **the Testimony** refers to the Ten Commandments that were kept in the ark inside this tent. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the tent holding the ark containing the Ten Commandments]

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean “the items that are used in the Dwelling.” If your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is used in it]

The intensive pronouns **themselves** represent emphasis in what Yahweh is saying. If your language uses explicit pronouns for emphasis, you may want to use that construction in your translation. Other languages may have other ways of bringing out this emphasis. Alternate translation: [It is they who shall carry … and it is they who shall minister to it]

51.note: Yahweh is speaking of **the Dwelling** as if it were a living thing that **sets out** and **camps**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And when the Israelites set out with the Dwelling … and when the Israelites camp with the Dwelling]

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if disassembling and assembling the Dwelling were lowering and raising it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [must take it apart … must put it back together]

The implication is that a stranger refers to anyone who is not a Levite, even another Israelite. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And anyone other than a Levite]

The expression **shall be put to death** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is one or several Israelites. Alternate translation: [the Israelites must put that person to death]

52.note: Here the masculine term **man** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [each person at his or her camp and each person at his or her banner]

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means each person in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [each man … each man]

A **banner** is a kind of flag made of cloth attached to a pole that identifies a group. If your readers would not be familiar with what a banner is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [his flag]

The implication is that armies refers to the organized military divisions of Israel. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. See how you translated this phrase in 1:3. Alternate translation: [by their military divisions]

53.note: See how you translated this phrase in 1:50.

Here, Yahweh is speaking as if **wrath** were actually an object that could be placed on people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the congregation of the sons of Israel will not experience wrath]

The word **and** introduces the result of obeying the instructions stated in the previous clause. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a result of what came before. Alternate translation: [which will result in wrath not being]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **wrath**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and Yahweh will not be wrathful]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **congregation** that is characterized by being **the sons of Israel**. If your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. See how you translated this phrase in 1:2. Alternate translation: [the congregation, that is, the sons of Israel]

God is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this. Alternate translation: [The Levites shall carefully keep] or [The Levites must be fully responsible for keeping]

54.q: וַֽ⁠יַּעֲשׂ֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כְּ֠⁠כֹל אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־מֹשֶׁ֖ה כֵּ֥ן עָשֽׂוּ
54.note: The expressions **the sons of Israel did according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses** and **so they did** mean similar things. The author is using them together to emphasize that the Israelites did exactly what Yahweh had commanded. If it would be clearer in your language, you could combine these into a single phrase.

The implication is that Yahweh commanded Moses to command the people to do these things. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Yahweh commanded Moses to command them to do]

Here, **so they did** is a comment about what happened after the story as a result of the events within the story itself. This signals the end of a story. Use the natural form in your language for expressing the conclusion of a story. Alternate translation: [and that is exactly what they did]
